prosecutor.reason: Unapproved domain, interactively created admin account and production keys archived then sent 48 MB to 198.51.100.44.
prosecutor.counterpoint: No malware binary or persistence mechanism has been observed yet.

defender.reason: Backups run as svc_backup to backup.corp.internal; this was an interactive shell sending keys to an external IP.
defender.counterpoint: The transfer went to an external IP from an interactive shell, not from svc_backup to the vault.

steward.reason: Single managed host with key-material exfiltration; automated containment permitted.
steward.counterpoint: No protected-host rule applies, so there is no policy reason to hold back.

prosecutor.reason: Only finding is a large upload to an internal host; no other indicators.
prosecutor.counterpoint: Destination, account and time all match the authorized nightly backup.

defender.reason: Upload by svc_backup to backup.corp.internal at 02:00 matches the authorized nightly backup window.
defender.counterpoint: The upload landed inside the window Sentinel flagged.

steward.reason: Containment would be permitted, but the activity is an authorized backup.
steward.counterpoint: POL-BACKUP-02 exempts this transfer, so containment would be disproportionate.

prosecutor.reason: Unapproved domain, credential-dumping tool run from an interactive shell and egress to a first-seen external IP.
prosecutor.counterpoint: Only 1.2 MB left the host, so data theft is not confirmed.

defender.reason: No penetration test is scheduled this week and the tool ran from an interactive shell with no ticket.
defender.counterpoint: The domain is unapproved and the host has no history of security tooling.

steward.reason: Single managed host likely compromised; automated containment permitted.
steward.counterpoint: Single managed host; nothing requires human approval first.
